also not any longer, not any more, no more, anymore

classical

Cic. Clu. 29: quem ōdisse jam nōn potestis (Lewis & Short s.v. jam)
Traupman 351

jam nōn

no longer, not any more

Says that something has stopped being so: jam nōn pluit, it’s not raining any more. So nihil jam, nothing any more; nēmō jam, nobody any more.

Other words

  • nōn diūtius — not for any longer time

    also used · classical · Traupman 88; Traupman 76

    Of something that will not go on: nōn diūtius manēbō, I won't stay any longer.

Examples

  • Theodōrus olīvam ē catīnō gustāvit, quae jam amāra nōn erat

    Theo tasted an olive from the dish, which was no longer bittercomposed

See also already, not yet, long.
